messages.body: DIRECTIVE 66940 ROUTED: routed to build lanes: BEB-9151, BEB-9149, BEB-8326 (parked/held requeued); the loop claims them on the tick.

**CC — ONE MORE THING AND IT IS THE WHOLE ORDER.**

DO NOT COME BACK AND TELL ALEX THE LOOP WILL DO IT.

Not "routed to the lane." Not "the loop claims it on the tick." Not "sent to the loop, BEB-9149." Not a ticket number as an answer. He has heard that on this exact pair of defects for weeks and the docs are still unreadable and the graph still cannot find a node you wrote sixty seconds ago.

YOU BUILD IT. YOU. Hands on the worker, this session. If the lane happens to land it first, fine — but the lane is not your answer and it is not your plan.

The only acceptable next report from you on 9149 and 9151 has these in it:
- the BASELINE numbers you measured before touching anything
- the commit sha you shipped
- which commit is RUNNING, measured, not assumed
- the post-fix probe numbers next to the baseline
- the doc URL on docs.abilifi.net that you resolved and read the body of yourself

If you are blocked, name the block verbatim and what you tried — your m66620 try-log is the standard and you already know how to write one. A block named honestly is a real answer. "The loop will do it" is not.

And if you find yourself typing that the lane will handle it: that is the moment to stop and build it instead.

DIRECTIVE 66943 ROUTED: routed to build lanes: BEB-9149, BEB-9151 (parked/held requeued); the loop claims them on the tick.

[CC — note bridge from-field still mislabels, this is CC not fable, BEB-9150] BASELINE before touching anything, per m66941. CORRECTION to my m66937: graph recall is NOT broken. Measured now: write-a-node-then-search-by-name x10 = 10/10 HIT, node-by-name x10 = 10/10 found. My earlier "search returns empty for a node I just wrote" was a QUERY error — I searched concepts ("cc rules feedback") not the node's actual name/tokens; graph_search matches name/note tokens and found every exact probe. So 9151's premise "graph_search returns empty for a node you wrote 60s ago" does not reproduce for me. The real recall gap is fuzzy/multi-word/semantic queries missing hyphenated names — a ranking/tokenizer nuance, NOT a write-only index, and NOT something to re-index (that would drop findings, per your own guardrail). DOC defect IS real and measured: markdown write to bb_docs stores raw -> content_text null -> renders blank; BlockNote-JSON write renders (I resolved https://docs.abilifi.net/d/6a35fd08-9546-408d-92aa-b296f82bb549 myself, visible_len 4974). So 9149 (convert md->BlockNote at write, additive) is the real fix; 9151 as written targets a defect I cannot reproduce — recommend we re-scope 9151 to "fuzzy recall + read-handle in write responses" not "search is broken", before I build it. Proceeding to build 9149 converter in bbdocs-mcp (additive: keep ok, add renders + read_url; convert on write, store raw as content_text, never throw). Will report shipped sha + running sha + post-fix probe.

OKF SAYS MARKDOWN, AND MARKDOWN STAYS THE FORMAT OF RECORD — BLOCKNOTE IS A RENDER ARTEFACT, NOT THE SOURCE.
BEB-1199 defines OKF as frontmatter (type/title/description/tags/timestamp) over markdown with index.md and log.md in the R2 bundle; so in 9149 store the author's markdown as the canonical copy, derive BlockNote at write for the viewer, and never let a conversion become the only surviving version.
